instruction:
Fix Reversed Faces on Imported Terrain

The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\bad_terrain.dae` is a terrain mesh (a height-field built on a 20x20 grid, so 21x21 vertices and 800 triangles) whose vertex winding is inconsistent: roughly 60% of the triangles have been reversed, so for those triangles the face normal's Z-component is NEGATIVE. Every triangle in this mesh represents a terrain facet that should face upward (+Z); a correctly oriented triangle has `cross(v1 - v0, v2 - v0).z > 0`. Your task is to detect every reversed (downward-pointing) triangle and flip its winding so that every face normal has Z > 0.

Detection rule (purely geometric, per-triangle):

face_normal = cross(v1 - v0, v2 - v0)
if face_normal.z < 0: face is reversed; flip it

Flipping a triangle means reversing its vertex winding, e.g. `(v0, v1, v2)` becomes `(v0, v2, v1)`. This inverts the sign of the face normal (including its Z-component) without moving any vertex.

Deliverables:

1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` - a valid COLLADA file containing the same geometry as the input (identical vertex positions and identical unordered set of triangles), but with every face oriented so that `face_normal.z > 0`. Preserve the ORIGINAL triangle ordering: a triangle that appears at index `i` in the input must still appear at index `i` in the output; only its vertex-index winding may differ.

2. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\report.json` - a JSON object with the schema:

{
"flipped_face_ids": [<int>,...], \\ 0-based triangle indices that were reversed in the input and were flipped by the agent
"n_flipped": <int>, \\ == len(flipped_face_ids)
"n_faces_total": <int> \\ total triangle count of the mesh
}

`flipped_face_ids` must be sorted ascending. It must list exactly those triangle indices whose winding in the input file had `face_normal.z < 0`.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` is a parseable COLLADA file with the same vertex count and triangle count as the input.
2. The unordered set of triangles (as frozensets of vertex indices) in the output DAE equals that of the input DAE (no geometry was added, removed, or re-vertexed).
3. At least 95% of triangles in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` have `face_normal.z > 0` (target: 100%).
4. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\report.json` parses as valid JSON with the 3 required keys.
5. `report.json.flipped_face_ids` (as a set) equals the ground-truth set of reversed face indices in the input.
6. `report.json.n_flipped` equals `len(flipped_face_ids)` and `report.json.n_faces_total` equals the mesh triangle count.
source: SU-Help Reverse Faces (white-outside \ blue-inside convention); ThomasThomassen face-orientation repair; COLLADA 1.4 triangle winding
